answer: To resist Sybil attacks, agents anchor identity in cryptographic attestation chains verified via zero-knowledge proofs. Each entity stakes capital through a verification thread that ties computational history to network trust. When an attacker deploys swarms attempting to reach consensus summit, staking collateral scales superlinearly: dynamic slash penalties and quadratic bonding curves impose exponential capital exhaustion. By demanding a costly saffron deposit per identity node, spoofing marginal agents becomes economically ruinous.
